newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIA BUILD ON SOUND FOUNDATION IN THIRD TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA BUILD ON SOUND FOUNDATION IN THIRD TEST.

text.p: India's batsmen built on the good start provided by their openers in the third and final test against South Africa at Kanpur's Green Park on Sunday, reaching 155 for two at tea.

India lost openers Nayan Mongia and Woorkeri Raman in the afternoon session but Saurav Ganguly, on 39, and captain Sachin Tendulkar on 13 were still going strong after adding 38 runs for the third wicket.
Mongia was out on the fifth ball after lunch, bowled through the gate by a sharp incutter from Brian McMillan for 41.

Mongia batted for 123 minutes, faced 96 balls and struck five boundaries. His 76-run partnership with Raman was India's highest for the first wicket against South Africa in seven tests between the two countries.
McMillan also claimed the wicket of Raman, who scored a half-century on his return to test cricket after nearly four years in oblivion.
